walkthroughs.body_html:
Characteristics & Classification — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Characteristics & Classification brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Characteristics & Classification.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The two-part Latin name of an organism is its:
options: family name
binomial name
domain
common name
Species
Genus
Kingdom
Class

mcqs.q: During an action potential, do Na+ and K+ move through the same channels?
options: Na+ and K+ swap places through the same channel at the same time.
Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
No — voltage-gated Na+ channels open first (depolarisation, Na+ in), then voltage-gated K+ channels open (repolarisation, K+ out).

mcqs.q: Do all arteries carry oxygenated blood?
options: Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.
All arteries carry oxygenated blood and all veins carry deoxygenated blood.
No — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.

mcqs.q: Where does transcription occur in a eukaryotic cell?
options: Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
Transcription happens on ribosomes in the cytoplasm.
Transcription happens in mitochondria where ATP is produced.
In the nucleus — DNA is transcribed to mRNA, which then travels to the cytoplasm.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Five-kingdom system”?
options: Linnaean groups: animals, plants, fungi, protists, prokaryotes.
Two-part Latin name: Genus species (e.g. Homo sapiens).
Grouping organisms by similarities to organise life and reflect evolution.
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species (broad → specific).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Species”?
options: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species (broad → specific).
Group of similar organisms that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.
Grouping organisms by similarities to organise life and reflect evolution.
Linnaean groups: animals, plants, fungi, protists, prokaryotes.
